proposals.announcement_evidence: display and processing hardware and test bed simulators used for Ship Self Defense System development
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the program itself, not a platform it supports: the deliverable is display/processing hardware and test-bed simulators for Ship Self Defense System work, and SSDS is a named member of BLI 5231's own narrative (Ship Missile Support Equipment, doc 333). SSDS appears exactly once in this org's index, so there is no alternative owner to confuse it with; the only textual gap is the singular/plural 'Ship' vs 'Ships', hence llm-alias rather than exact-name. Money color is partly congruent: the paragraph obligates fiscal 2016 other procurement (Navy) alongside fiscal 2016 RDT&E, and 5231 is an OPN line. The residual risk a refute lens should weigh is that 5231 is a multi-program equipment line (AEGIS, MK 57 VLS, RHIMES all sit in it) and that prototype test articles for 'development' could belong to the RDT&E share instead.

refute_a.reason: Money and mission both hold: the paragraph names fiscal 2016 other procurement (Navy) and 5231 is an OPN line, and the deliverable - display/processing hardware and test bed simulators - is literally the content of a line titled Ship Missile Support Equipment, with SSDS named in that line's own narrative; SSDS is a combat system, not a platform the contract merely supports, and the multi-name line is a system family, not a §3 catch-all (the RDT&E share of $1,440,073 is the minority and does not move the action off the procurement line).

refute_b.reason: "Ships Self Defense System (SSDS)" appears exactly once in the N index (row 1955, BLI 5231) and the announcement names that program by its own official wording, so no other PE owns the name; the only near-neighbour, "Self Defense Test Ship (SDTS)" at 0605863N, is a different program (a test ship, not the combat system) and the paragraph never mentions it, and the singular/plural "Ship"/"Ships" gap is the real J-book spelling of one program, not an invented alias.

proposals.announcement_evidence: integration services for mission packages that will deploy from and integrate with littoral combat ships
proposals.rationale: The sole-source award is mission-package integration for littoral combat ships across MCM, littoral ASW and littoral SUW - that is the LCS Mission Modules program's own work, not a platform the contract merely supports, and PE 0603596N is titled 'LCS Mission Modules'. 'Mission package' and 'mission module' are the program's own paired terms (a package is the module plus its crew and aircraft), so the alias is real rather than invented. The honest weakness for the refute lenses: three lines in this index own mission-module names - 0603596N (RDT&E), 1600 (LCS Common Mission Modules Equipment, OPN) and 1601 (LCS MCM Mission Modules, OPN) - and the queued paragraph is cut off before its funding sentence, so the appropriation that would separate them is not visible in the text; the cost-plus-fixed-fee integration-services form is what points at the RDT&E line.

refute_a.reason: The appropriation sentence is cut off, but a 2015 sole-source cost-plus-fixed-fee mission-package integration award for packages still in development (MCM, littoral ASW, littoral SUW) is RDT&E-shaped work, not O&M sustainment and not an OPN hardware buy, so it sits on the right side of lens A's failure mode; the named thing is the mission-package program itself, with the littoral combat ship appearing only as the host, and PE 0603596N 'LCS Mission Modules' is a program PE rather than a rollup - the OPN siblings 1600/1601 are an alternative-owner question for lens B, not a money break.

refute_b.reason: Four PEs in this index own mission-module/mission-package names — 0603596N (LCS Mission Modules), 1600 (LCS Common Mission Modules Equipment), 1601 (LCS MCM Mission Modules) and 1603 (LCS SUW Mission Modules) — and the paragraph's own words ("mission packages" for mine countermeasures, littoral ASW and littoral surface warfare, deploying from littoral combat ships) enumerate the mission areas 1601 and 1603 are named for while offering nothing that selects the RDT&E line; worse, the index itself splits the two wordings the proposal equates, assigning "Mission Package" rows and "Mission Modules" rows to different PEs, so "mission packages" → "Mission Modules (MM)" is exactly the mapping the lexicon contradicts, and the record text is truncated before any funding sentence that could break the tie.

proposals.announcement_evidence: to exercise options to procure onboard repair parts for Virginia class attack submarines Pre Commissioning Unit (PCU) Arkansas (SSN 800) and PCU Utah (SSN 801)
proposals.rationale: Onboard repair parts bought for two named pre-commissioning Virginia-class hulls are part of those ships' own construction cost, and the paragraph says the money is fiscal 2018 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) - the appropriation of BLI 2013, an SCN line (doc 341) whose title is the program named. proposals.rationale: Constellation class is the class name of FFG 62, so the announcement and the index row name the same ship class rather than two resembling strings, and the work - engineering and class services for detail design and construction - is the frigate line's own content, performed by the lead-ship builder. proposals.announcement_evidence: 969 AN/APX-123A(V) IFF transponders to include 777 for the Navy, 101 for the Army, two for the Coast Guard
proposals.rationale: The delivery order buys the designated item itself - AN/APX-123A(V) normalizes to the AN/APX-123 CXP that BLI 2851 'ID Systems' names in its own narrative - so the claim is about the program's equipment, not a platform it rides on. Remaining exposure for lens A: the paragraph is cut off before its funding sentence, so the OPN color of 2851 cannot be confirmed from the text alone and should be checked against the lake, and 14 of the transponders are a Bahrain FMS variant (AN/APX-117A) that this line does not fund.

refute_b.reason: This is a live same-designator collision: two PEs in the index own AN/APX-123 — 2851 "AN/APX-123 Common Digital Transponder (CXP)" and 3620 "AN/APX-123" (Coast Guard Equipment, not a catch-all and therefore publishable) — and the normalized designator the proposal relies on matches 3620's row as a whole string while matching 2851's only as a prefix; the paragraph contains none of 2851's distinguishing words (no "Common Digital Transponder", no "CXP", no "ID Systems"), the quantity split is a share argument rather than an identity one, and the order in fact spans a second designator (14 AN/APX-117A for Bahrain) plus six other FMS customers, so the same evidence attaches to more than one owner.

proposals.announcement_evidence: contract N00024-19-D-4323 for the Emergency Ship Salvage Material system
proposals.rationale: The announcement spells the program out in full - 'the Emergency Ship Salvage Material system' - which is verbatim the name BLI 1130 'Diving and Salvage Equipment' owns in its own narrative, and the identically-abbreviated 'Evolved Sea Sparrow Missile (ESSM)' at 6120 cannot be confused with it because the words are written out. refute_a.reason: REFUTED on money: the action obligates nothing at all - it only raises an IDIQ ordering ceiling from $280,000,000 to $318,000,000 with all funding deferred to future task orders - so it paid for none of this line's work, and the cost-plus-award-fee/cost-plus-fixed-fee structure with work 'at other locations worldwide according to future delivery orders' is the ESSM base-network operation and maintenance vehicle, i.e. O&M-colored logistics and base-operations services (§3 generic services) attached to an OPN line that procures diving and salvage equipment - precisely the sustainment-on-a-procurement-line failure mode the 2026-09-04 held-out study found.

refute_b.reason: The announcement writes the program out in full — "the Emergency Ship Salvage Material system" — which is verbatim row 1278 of the index and the only owner of that name; the identically-abbreviated "Evolved Sea Sparrow Missile (ESSM)" at 2307 and 6120 cannot be reached from spelled-out words, no variant or increment is in play, and the evidence is the contract's stated subject rather than the contractor's name (Global PCCI appears only as the awardee).
